html:
Thebes is the chief city of Boeotia in central Greece, north west of Athens, and was one of the great powers of the Greek world. For a short time in the 4th century BCE it was the strongest city in Greece.

It was already a major palace centre in Mycenaean times, and Greek myth set many stories there: Cadmus and the founding of the city, Dionysus and Heracles, and the tragedy of Oedipus. The poet Pindar was a Theban.

Thebes sided with Persia in 480 BCE, which Athens never forgot, and usually led the league of Boeotian cities. Sparta seized its citadel in 382 BCE, after the King's Peace had broken up the league. Theban exiles freed it three years later. Under Epaminondas and Pelopidas, with the elite Sacred Band, Thebes crushed Sparta at the Battle of Leuctra in 371 BCE and freed Messenia. Its lead faded after Epaminondas fell in battle in 362 BCE.

It then led the Third Sacred War against Phocis and in 338 BCE stood with Athens against Philip of Macedon at the Battle of Chaeronea, where the Sacred Band was wiped out. When Thebes revolted after Philip's death, Alexander destroyed the city in 335 BCE, sparing only the temples and Pindar's house. Cassander rebuilt it in 316 BCE, but it never regained its power.
sum: Thebes is the chief city of Boeotia in central Greece, north west of Athens, and was one of the great powers of the Greek world. For a short time in the 4th century BCE it was the strongest city in Greece.
